summary: As of mid-2026, ChatGPT/GPT models retain the largest consumer mindshare with 55.5% of generative AI web visits, but the enterprise API market has fragmented significantly with Anthropic leading at 40% of enterprise API usage versus OpenAI at 27% and Google at 21%. Open-source models from DeepSeek, Meta, Qwen, and Kimi have closed the gap dramatically with frontier closed-source models, with DeepSeek alone capturing 24.4% of OpenRouter text requests. The competitive landscape now spans dozens of major LLMs, with the battle centering on reasoning, coding, and agentic capabilities.

models.name: GPT-5 / GPT-5.1
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT holds 55.5% of worldwide generative AI web visits as of August 2026 (Similarweb), and OpenAI leads LLM API provider rankings per Future AGI, commanding 27% of enterprise API usage.
strengths: Largest developer ecosystem and tooling integrations
Strong general-purpose reasoning and instruction following
Broad multimodal capabilities
Extensive enterprise deployment track record
Widest third-party plugin and API integration support
models.best_for: General-purpose enterprise applications, consumer-facing chatbots, and broad API integrations

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1 / Claude Opus 5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic leads enterprise API usage at 40% market share (Menlo Ventures 2026), and Claude recorded 952.6 million web visits in May 2026, up 855% year-over-year; Claude Fable 5.1 tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 66.
strengths: Leads enterprise API adoption with 40% market share
Top score on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (66)
Exceptional long-context document understanding
Strong safety and alignment properties
Best-in-class coding and reasoning benchmarks among closed models
models.best_for: Enterprise API workloads, complex document analysis, coding assistance, and safety-critical deployments

models.name: Gemini 3 Family (Flash / Pro)
models.popularity_notes: Google Gemini reached 2.9 billion web visits in May 2026 (450% YoY growth per Similarweb) and holds 25.6% of generative AI web traffic and 21% of enterprise API usage as of August 2026.
strengths: Fastest-growing platform with 450% YoY web traffic growth
Industry-leading context window up to 1M+ tokens
Strong multimodal and code generation performance
Deep integration with Google Cloud and Workspace
Competitive Flash tier for cost-sensitive deployments
models.best_for: Long-context multimodal tasks, Google Cloud-native deployments, and cost-optimized high-volume inference

models.name: DeepSeek-V4 / DeepSeek-V4-Pro
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek captures 24.4% of OpenRouter text API requests as of September 2026 and holds 3.4% of global generative AI web visits; DeepSeek-V4-Pro ranks at the top of the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard for bug fixing, code generation, and reasoning.
strengths: 24.4% of OpenRouter API requests showing massive developer adoption
Top-ranked open-source model for bug fixing and code generation (Onyx Leaderboard)
Developed with significantly less compute than comparable models
Strong reasoning and tool-use capabilities
Open weights with permissive licensing enabling self-hosting
models.best_for: Cost-conscious coding workloads, self-hosted deployments, and high-volume API usage requiring open-source flexibility

models.name: Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: Meta Llama 4 ranks as the top open-source LLM for general reasoning per multiple 2026 leaderboards, and the Llama family consistently leads HuggingFace download statistics with hundreds of millions of cumulative downloads across variants.
strengths: Largest open-source model community and ecosystem
Top HuggingFace download counts across the model family
Highly flexible for fine-tuning and custom deployment
Strong general reasoning capabilities among open models
Extensive third-party tooling support (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp)
models.best_for: Self-hosted general-purpose deployments, fine-tuning for domain-specific tasks, and research applications

models.name: Qwen 3 / Qwen 2.5 Family
models.popularity_notes: The Qwen family has been adopted by over 90,000 enterprises across consumer electronics, gaming, and other sectors, and Qwen3.6-27B ranks among the top open-source models for code generation on the Onyx Leaderboard.
strengths: Adopted by 90,000+ enterprises worldwide
Best-in-class multilingual capabilities across 100+ languages
Strong performance on code generation benchmarks
Apache 2.0 / MIT licensing for commercial use
Wide range of model sizes for varied deployment needs
models.best_for: Multilingual enterprise applications, global product deployments, and coding tasks requiring open commercial licensing

models.name: Grok-4
models.popularity_notes: Grok holds 2.4% of global generative AI web visits as of August 2026 (Similarweb) and ranks among the top 5 most-used LLMs in 2026 per Exploding Topics and Zapier rankings, with deep integration into X (Twitter) driving significant reach.
strengths: Real-time information access via X platform integration
Strong reasoning and multimodal capabilities
Top-5 placement in major 2026 LLM adoption rankings
Competitive performance on math and coding benchmarks
Unique real-time social media data access
models.best_for: Real-time information retrieval, social media analytics, and reasoning tasks requiring up-to-date knowledge

models.name: Kimi-K2.6 / Kimi K3
models.popularity_notes: Kimi-K2.6 sets a new open-source bar on SWE-Bench Verified and GPQA Diamond benchmarks, ranking among the top open-source models for reasoning and coding on the Onyx Leaderboard, with benchmark results competitive with GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6.
strengths: State-of-the-art long-horizon coding and agentic performance
Competitive with top closed-source models on SWE-Bench Verified (~80%)
Strong generalization across niche programming languages including Zig
Top open-source reasoning scores on Onyx Leaderboard
Sustains long autonomous coding sessions across full-stack domains
models.best_for: Complex autonomous coding tasks, agentic software engineering, and long-horizon development workflows

models.name: Mistral Large / Mistral Small 4
models.popularity_notes: Mistral ranks among the top open-source LLMs for speed and efficiency in 2026 per multiple leaderboards, with Mistral Small 4 (119B MoE, 6.5B active parameters) offering frontier-level instruction following, reasoning, and coding at $0.15/$0.60 per 1M tokens under Apache 2.0.
strengths: Best price-to-performance ratio among MoE open models
Apache 2.0 licensing for unrestricted commercial use
Strong European data sovereignty compliance
Efficient MoE architecture (only 6.5B active params at inference)
Competitive reasoning and coding in a cost-optimized package
models.best_for: Cost-optimized production deployments, European compliance-sensitive applications, and high-throughput inference workloads

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.popularity_notes: MiniMax M3 ranks among the top open-source models for bug fixing and code generation on the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard (updated July 2026), clustering tightly with DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Kimi-K2.6 within a few benchmark points on SWE-Bench Verified and GPQA Diamond.
strengths: Top-tier open-source performance on bug fixing benchmarks
Exceptionally large 1M token context window
Competitive with frontier models on GPQA Diamond
Strong code generation rankings alongside DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi
MIT/Apache licensing enabling broad commercial deployment
models.best_for: Large-scale document processing, code review at scale, and long-context reasoning tasks requiring open-source flexibility
